description: Three iOS-only UX surfaces on eb-branch. (1) Modernize the Settings sheet for visual consistency. (2) Make the customizable quick-button row ('custom keyboard') clearer to configure + add a hold-for-all-slash-commands palette. (3) Reduce Quip-vocabulary mangling in the PTT voice->text pipeline on BOTH the local SFSpeech and remote Mac-Whisper paths. ALL work is iOS-only (QuipiOS) with NO Mac rebuild and NO persistence schema change (quickSlotsJSON / customButtonsJSON unchanged). The strongest voice fix (Mac Whisper initial_prompt biasing) is a deferred follow-up because it needs a Mac rebuild. Source spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-16-settings-modernize-keyboard-ux-design.md. Native: gate = xcodebuild (QuipiOS, Swift-6 mode) succeeds + the noted unit tests compile/pass; on-device/manual verify is the user's pass (note it in the story). NEVER push eb-branch without an explicit literal 'push'.

userStories.title: Settings row visual consistency
userStories.description: As a user, I want every Settings row to share one modern visual style so the page looks consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a trailing-@ViewBuilder overload settingsLinkRow<Trailing: View>(title:subtitle:systemImage:tint:trailing:) so a row can supply a trailing view instead of only a String (QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift, helper at :5983)
Convert the Latency row (:5837) to the tinted-chip helper, passing the LatencySummary().badgeView() as the trailing view
Convert the Version button (:5856) to the tinted-chip helper (info.circle), preserving its tap-to-copy + 'Copied' confirmation transition
Leave macPermsSection unchanged (its red/green semantics are intentional)
xcodebuild (QuipiOS) succeeds
Manual (user verify): Settings -> Diagnostics shows Latency + Version with the standard chip; badge intact; Version still copies
userStories.notes: Added @ViewBuilder trailing overload of settingsLinkRow (QuipApp.swift); Latency row now passes LatencySummary.badgeView() through it; Version button uses the helper (info.circle) keeping tap-to-copy + 'Copied' .transition(.opacity). macPermsSection untouched. Gate: xcodebuild QuipiOS BUILD SUCCEEDED (generic iOS Simulator, Swift-6). Manual on-device verify is the user's pass. NOTE: the dedicated Quip QA sim UDID 3B2ACF04-… is now GONE too — only available sim is iPhone 17 Pro CFCE8360-508E-4A66-B0FD-615D8CD2A549 (OS 26.5); used generic/platform=iOS Simulator for the compile gate.

userStories.title: Custom-button add-key clarity
userStories.description: As a user, I want it to be obvious how to add a custom key and what it will look like.
acceptanceCriteria: CustomButtonForm (QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift:7063) shows a LIVE pill preview at the top, reusing the customQuickButton chrome (:4412), updating as the user types
Label auto-fills from the payload when empty (slash -> command text, text -> first ~8 chars, keystroke -> option label); an explicit label is never overwritten
Per-type explanatory footers: Slash (auto-submit guidance + a tip that same-first-letter slash keys auto-group into a /x... menu), Text, Keystroke
SF Symbol field gets a placeholder example (e.g. bolt.fill) + an optional/falls-back-to-label note
QuickButtonsSheet empty-state / add entry copy clearly points at '+ -> Custom Button'
No change to customButtonsJSON wire format
xcodebuild (QuipiOS) succeeds
Manual (user verify): + -> Custom Button, type a slash -> preview + label update live; footers visible; Save -> pill appears and fires
userStories.notes: CustomButtonForm (QuipApp.swift) now opens with a top 'Preview' section rendering a live previewPill that mirrors the customQuickButton chrome (9pt mono label / 16x16 symbol on the tinted chip via QuipColors chipFill+chipText). Label auto-fills from the payload (slash->command word, text->first ~8 chars, keystroke->option label) via labelEdited gate: the Label TextField writes through a custom Binding that sets labelEdited on a real edit, while autofillLabelIfNeeded() writes label directly on .onChange(of: text/keystroke/payloadKind); clearing the field re-enables auto-fill; hydrate() marks an existing label explicit so edit never clobbers. Action section converted to header/footer form with a per-type actionFooter (Slash: auto-submit guidance + the /x... same-first-letter auto-group tip; Text; Keystroke). SF Symbol placeholder now 'SF Symbol e.g. bolt.fill (optional)' + a Label-section footer noting blank->auto-fill and symbol-replaces-label. QuickButtonsSheet empty state now reads 'Tap + -> Custom Button...' and the add sheet's first section gained a footer pointing at Custom Button. No customButtonsJSON wire change (CustomButton/CustomPayload untouched). Gate: xcodebuild QuipiOS (generic/platform=iOS Simulator, Swift-6) ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **. Manual on-device verify (type a slash -> preview + label update live; footers visible; Save -> pill appears and fires) is the user's pass per PRD.

userStories.title: Hold-any-slash-key slash palette
userStories.description: As a user, I want to hold any slash key to pick from all slash commands, not only when two share a first letter.
acceptanceCriteria: In slotRowView (QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift:4241), slash-category pills (built-in isSlashCommand and custom .slash) get a long-press Menu / .contextMenu listing ALL slash commands (built-in slash QuickButtons + custom .slash buttons)
Menu items fire via the existing fireQuickButton / fireCustomButton; reuse SlashGroupMember (:4085) as the element type
Primary single-tap behavior of each pill is unchanged
Palette is NOT attached to answer/keystroke pills (slash-only gesture meaning)
Accessibility hint 'Long-press for all slash commands' on slash pills
Existing auto-grouping (/x... tap-menu) still works; horizontal row scroll is NOT degraded by the long-press gesture (prior gesture-conflict precedent at :6419)
xcodebuild (QuipiOS) succeeds
Manual (user verify): long-press a lone /plan pill -> menu of all slash commands -> tap /compact fires it; single tap still fires /plan; row still scrolls
userStories.notes: Added two helpers in QuipApp.swift before slotRowView: allSlashMembers() returns the full slash set — QuickButton.allCases.filter(\.isSlashCommand) (built-ins, incl. bare '/') + every custom .slash button — INDEPENDENT of the row (the palette's point is reaching unpinned commands; the existing /x… tap-menu still only groups same-first-letter pills on the row). slashPalette<Content: View>(_:) wraps a pill with .contextMenu listing allSlashMembers(), each firing via the existing fireQuickButton/fireCustomButton (reusing SlashGroupMember as the element type), plus accessibilityHint 'Long-press for all slash commands'. slotRowView now wraps .builtinButton pills with slashPalette ONLY when b.isSlashCommand, and .customButton pills ONLY when payload is .slash — answer/keystroke pills get nothing (slash-only gesture). .slashGroup left untouched so its /x… tap-menu is unchanged. Chose .contextMenu over a manual LongPressGesture/.simultaneousGesture so the horizontal ScrollView pan is never stolen (system context-menu recognizer yields to an in-progress scroll) — satisfies the no-scroll-degradation + gesture-conflict-precedent criterion. Primary single-tap unchanged (Button action). No wire-format / persistence change. Gate: xcodebuild QuipiOS (generic/platform=iOS Simulator, Swift-6) ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **. Manual on-device verify (long-press a lone /plan -> menu of all slash commands -> tap /compact fires it; single tap still fires /plan; row still scrolls) is the user's pass per PRD.

userStories.title: Expand PTT dictation vocabulary
userStories.description: As a user, I want the local on-device recognizer biased toward Quip vocabulary so common dev terms stop mangling.
acceptanceCriteria: QuipiOS/Resources/dictation-vocab.txt expanded with the demonstrably-mangled + working vocabulary: slash-command stems (compact, plan, clear, prd, caveman, ultrareview), agent names (Codex, Grok, Cursor, Kokoro), Simulator, keystroke, Xcodegen, entitlements, APNs, keychain, devicectl, Tailscale (confirm present), monospace (confirm present)
File stays one-term-per-line plain text (loaded by DictationVocab.loadBundled(), applied as request.contextualStrings at SpeechService:620 and :774)
No code change required beyond the resource (verify it is in the QuipiOS bundle/Resources build phase)
xcodebuild (QuipiOS) succeeds
Manual (user verify, local path = disconnected): on-device dictation of the new terms improves
userStories.notes: Appended 17 new bias terms to QuipiOS/Resources/dictation-vocab.txt (20->37 lines, well under DictationVocab.maxTerms=100): slash stems compact/plan/clear/prd/caveman/ultrareview, agents Codex/Grok/Cursor/Kokoro, plus Simulator/keystroke/Xcodegen/entitlements/APNs/keychain/devicectl. Tailscale (line 17) + monospace (line 6) confirmed already present, NOT duplicated. File stays one-term-per-line plain text. NOTE: DictationVocab.load (SpeechService.swift:9) trims+drops-blank lines but has NO comment syntax, so every non-blank line ships as a contextualStrings bias string — kept it pure vocab (no '#' headers). No code change: Resources/ is a folder-ref that globs into the QuipiOS Copy-Bundle-Resources phase, so the edited file auto-ships (verified: the freshly built Quip.app/dictation-vocab.txt has all 37 terms incl. devicectl/Codex/ultrareview/Tailscale/monospace). loadBundled() -> request.contextualStrings at SpeechService:620 (live) + :774 (remote-handoff request). Gate: xcodebuild QuipiOS (generic/platform=iOS Simulator, Swift-6) ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **. Manual on-device dictation verify (local/disconnected path) is the user's pass per PRD.

userStories.title: TranscriptCorrector for both PTT paths
userStories.description: As a user, I want Quip terms corrected even on the remote Whisper path that has no biasing, since that's the path I hit when connected.
acceptanceCriteria: New QuipiOS/Services/TranscriptCorrector.swift: a value type holding a curated map of high-confidence mishearings -> canonical Quip terms (e.g. 'tail scale'->'Tailscale', 'mono type'->'monospace', 'x code'->'Xcode', 'web socket'->'WebSocket', 'co-dex'->'Codex')
Matching is case-insensitive, whole-word/phrase (word-boundary) only, preserves surrounding text AND the leading/trailing whitespace the send pipeline relies on
Applied to the FINAL transcript only (not partials) at the convergence point in SpeechService (the onUpdateCallback(..., isFinal:true) delivery at :711)

FIRST confirm the remote path (client.onTranscriptResult at SpeechService:98) flows through that same final sink; if it has a separate exit, apply the corrector there too so the remote Whisper output is corrected
Conservative: only entries unambiguous in a Quip/dev context; never remap a token that is a common English word in normal use
New QuipiOS/Tests/TranscriptCorrectorTests.swift: assert the captured mangling examples map to canonical terms AND that non-Quip prose passes through untouched
xcodebuild (QuipiOS) succeeds; tests compile/pass
Manual (user verify, connected = remote path): PTT a sentence with Tailscale/monospace/Codex -> transcript shows canonical spelling; ordinary dictation unchanged
